The US FDA has approved Roche
-owned Genentech's Tecentriq (atezolizumab) as an adjuvant treatment for Stage III mismatch repair deficient (dMMR) colon cancer in adults and children two years and older.
The indication is for Tecentriq and Tecentriq Hybreza in combination with a fluoropyrimidine and oxaliplatin.

Approval was based on the results of the phase 3 ATOMIC/ML39057 randomized, open-label, active-controlled trial that enrolled patients after they had a complete resection of the primary tumor with no evidence of residual lymph node involvement or metastatic disease. Participants were randomized to receive either Tecentriq plus mFOLFOX6 (oxaliplatin, leucovorin, and fluorouracil) for 12 cycles followed by Tecentriq alone for six months or mFOLFOX6 alone for 12 cycles.
The Tecentriq regimen improved disease-free survival better than the mFOLFOX6 alone treatment.
The FDA's review was conducted under the agency's Project Orbis initiative, with regulators in Australia, Canada, Israel, and Switzerland taking part.

title: Genentech's Tecentriq gains new indication for colon cancer
